sentences.text: Azure AI Search stores your documents in an index, like the index of a book but smarter.
You connect that index to your agent and it answers with your own documents.
It is like giving it a tidy filing cabinet, instead of asking it to guess.
Copilot Studio supports vectorized indexes with integrated vectorization.
The same embeddings model that vectorized the data also vectorizes the user question.
It also supports the semantic ranker, but that improvement is configured earlier in Azure, not in Copilot Studio.
This way the search understands meaning.
You add it from Add knowledge, in Featured, or from the properties of a Generative answers node.
There are four authentication types: Access Key, client certificate, Service principal, and integrated Entra I D.
Only one vector index per connection.
You will see the progress on screen.
To get citations, the index must include a field with the real address of the document.
If metadata storage path exists, it is used as the citation.
Users also need access to the cited documents.
Without that field, the answer appears without a link to the original document.
If they ask you to connect Azure OpenAI on your data, it is not a knowledge source: you use Classic data in the node.
And if they ask you to provision the semantic ranker from Copilot Studio, that is wrong: it is configured in Azure.
Write it down for the exam.
